Paper · 29 Jan 2025

Abundant ammonia and nitrogen-rich organic matter in asteroid Bennu

Glavin, Dworkin, Alexander, Aponte et al. (62 authors) · Nature Astronomy 9:199-210

In a sentence

33 amino acids, 14 of the 20 used by life, and all five nucleobases in pristine Bennu samples; the chiral amino acids show no handedness bias.

In plain words

NASA's OSIRIS-REx brought back dust and pebbles from asteroid Bennu, kept away from Earth's air and life. They hold 33 amino acids, 14 of them used in proteins, all five DNA and RNA bases and lots of ammonia. Amino acids come in left- and right-handed forms; life uses only left-handed ones. The Bennu amino acids whose handedness could be measured come in equal amounts, which weakens the idea that meteorites gave Earth its bias.

Technical detail

Bennu is richer in carbon, nitrogen and ammonia than Ryugu and most meteorites; 15N enrichments point to a cold outer-disc origin. 33 amino acids identified plus unidentified C6-C7 aliphatic ones; at least 23 N-heterocycles including all five canonical nucleobases; about 10,000 N-bearing species. All enantiomerically resolvable chiral non-protein amino acids (e.g. isovaline, norvaline) were racemic or near racemic, and racemic alanine and aspartic acid indicate negligible contamination.

What we take from it

Planned test

Building blocks were common in the early Solar System; the racemic result counts against a meteoritic origin of life's handedness. Feeds task #11.

Source checked against its DOI. Read the original.
